Title: A comprehensive survey of research towards AI-enabled unmanned aerial systems in pre-, active-, and post-wildfire management
Principal_Scope: AI-enabled UAS across pre-, active-, and post-wildfire management
Relationship_to_this_review: The closest fire-specific technical review, but organised around wildfire-management stages and AI/UAV technologies rather than the smoke-specific chain from observation and forecasting through exposure, health risk, communication and protective action.
Claim_Boundary: Scope comparison only; not deployment evidence

Title: A comprehensive review of plume source detection using unmanned vehicles for environmental sensing
Principal_Scope: Environmental sensing and plume-source localisation using autonomous unmanned vehicles, including atmospheric dispersion, source localisation and plume-interface tracking.
Relationship_to_this_review: Provides transferable evidence for plume localisation and tracking, but is not wildfire-specific and does not extend into population-health interpretation or protective action.

Title: Gas source localization and mapping with mobile robots: A review
Principal_Scope: Mobile-robot gas sensing, source localisation and gas-distribution mapping in controlled and uncontrolled environments.
Relationship_to_this_review: Provides transferable evidence for mobile gas localisation and mapping, but does not validate these methods specifically for wildfire smoke or connect them to downstream health and response.

Title: Unmanned aerial vehicles and low-cost sensors for air quality monitoring: A comprehensive review of applications across diverse emission sources
Principal_Scope: UAV and low-cost-sensor air-quality monitoring across diverse emission sources, with attention to spatial and temporal measurement, calibration, sensor reliability and UAV-induced measurement effects.
Relationship_to_this_review: Closely relevant to mobile air-quality sensing, including biomass-burning applications, but does not synthesise uncontrolled-wildfire response from forecasting through health interpretation and protective action.
Claim_Boundary: Scope positioning only; no fire-validation inference

Title: Critical review of health impacts of wildfire smoke exposure
Principal_Scope: Epidemiological evidence on wildfire-smoke health effects, including mortality and respiratory, cardiovascular, mental and perinatal outcomes, together with susceptible populations.
Relationship_to_this_review: Establishes the wildfire-smoke health-effects literature, but does not examine how real-time sensing and forecasting are translated into operational health-risk estimates, communication or intervention.
Claim_Boundary: Scope comparison and health-evidence synthesis only

Title: A scoping review of wildfire smoke risk communications: issues, gaps, and recommendations
Principal_Scope: Wildfire-smoke risk communication, including communication materials, dissemination strategies, behaviour change, vulnerable populations and health literacy.
Relationship_to_this_review: Examines the communication end of the problem, but not upstream sensing and plume forecasting; smoke-plume satellite and remote-sensing studies and health-outcome studies were outside its inclusion scope.
Claim_Boundary: Scope comparison and communication-evidence synthesis only
